label: Toggle
title: Toggle
summary: Use a Toggle to switch one setting on or off, with the change taking effect straight away.
corePrinciple: One setting, one switch, and the change happens at once.

anatomy.title: A track and a thumb
anatomy.description: Toggle is 52 × 31 px with fully rounded ends. Off, the track is grey with the thumb on the left; on, it turns purple and the thumb slides right.

configuration.title: One size, labelled by its row
configuration.description: Toggle has no size or style options. It has no label of its own, so it always sits at the end of a row whose title names the setting.

sizing.title: Always 52 × 31 px
sizing.description: The toggle never stretches. The track is 52 × 31 px with 3 px padding around a 25 px thumb, so give its row at least 31 px of height.

content.title: Name the setting, not the action
content.description: The row’s title says what the toggle controls, such as “Payment alerts”. Don’t write “Turn on” or “Enable”: the switch already shows on or off.

inContext.title: A settings card
inContext.description: Each change applies as soon as the toggle moves. The screen keeps every value and saves it; the toggle only reports the new value.
blocks: Payment alerts on · Biometric login off · Hide balances off

sources.title: Use the public Toggle contract
sources.description: The guide compares the Figma component with the installed package and its Storybook stories.
blocks: Installed jfs-components is 0.1.78 (12 October build) from the team’s private package repository. Figma has two variants, Off and On, both 52 × 31; the package adds disabled, which dims the toggle to 50% and greys the track in both states. Toggle has no label of its own, so the screen names it, usually with the row’s title. On the web it is a switch with a name, and its on or off state is announced. Enter, Space, and click switch it. A disabled toggle is announced as disabled and skipped by Tab.
